note: Regression fixture built from a real 19-scene Columbus visual plan. Scene 3 carries a stray CJK character, scene 13 leaks the StyleConstraints field name into a slot, and the narration uses three unexplained hard words (mutiny, Genoese, uncharted).
story: Columbus stood on the deck of a small wooden ship. The crew had not seen land for many days. They were tired, hungry, and very afraid. Some sailors began to talk about a mutiny, and their voices grew loud. Genoa was his home, and Genoese ships were his life. He wanted to reach Asia by sailing west across the ocean. Most scholars thought the sea was too wide for such a voyage. He asked the king and queen of Spain for ships and money. They refused him at first, then changed their minds. In August of fourteen ninety-two, three ships left the harbour. The voyage was long, and the wind fell still for days. The sailors watched an uncharted sea stretch to the horizon. Columbus kept two logs, one for the crew and one for himself. A small bird flew past the ship and the crew took hope. On the twelfth of October, a sailor called out that he saw land. They reached an island where people already lived. Columbus named the island San Salvador and claimed it for Spain. He sailed on to other islands, still sure he had reached Asia. He never found the gold cities he promised, but the world he opened changed everything.

claims.claim: Columbus was born in Genoa and sailed for Spain.
The voyage left Spain in August 1492 with three ships.
The crew came close to mutiny during the long crossing.
Columbus promised gold cities and never found them.
